title: Dell Shields Business from AI Bust With Just in Time Model

tickers.name: SK hynix Inc. American Depositary Shares

summary:
Dell Technologies is fulfilling a $95 billion backlog of AI servers through a customer-funded delivery system that limits the company's inventory exposure. CEO Michael Dell stated that utilizing just-in-time manufacturing and a negative cash conversion cycle creates a financial cushion to survive a potential downturn in AI spending, unlike the model used by more heavily indebted infrastructure providers. This approach currently serves over 6,500 AI customers and supports a projected 70% increase in fiscal-year revenue.

Michael Dell also warned that memory chip shortages will intensify next year, with DRAM supply continuing to restrict deliveries. While some market participants express concern over a memory oversupply by 2027 that has weighed on Micron and SK Hynix, Dell noted that new fabrication plants are unlikely to provide meaningful relief until 2029 or 2030.

MICHAEL DELL REVEALS HOW HIS COMPANY COULD SURVIVE AN AI BUST

Dell Technologies ($DELL ) is positioning itself to withstand a potential AI downturn through just-in-time manufacturing and a negative cash conversion cycle.

Unlike heavily indebted AI infrastructure providers, Dell largely builds servers against customer orders, limiting inventory exposure.

•  AI server backlog: $95 billion
•  AI customers: 6,500+
•  Projected fiscal-year revenue growth: 70%

However, Michael Dell warns that memory chip shortages could worsen next year.

The key takeaway: Dell's customer-funded operating model may offer protection against an AI spending slowdown, although weaker demand could quickly hit revenue.
